text: Deep in the dense forests between Kiang and the Casamance border, where foreign maps showed only green wilderness, rose the fortified citadel of Medina.
Foday Kaba Dumbuya did not build with soft mud that washed away in the August rains.
He felled thousands of massive mahogany and ironwood trees, driving them two fathoms into the earth in double parallel palisades packed with red clay and broken river rock.
Behind these walls lived blacksmiths forging muskets, scholars teaching the Quran, and cavalrymen who could ride through mangrove mud without leaving a trace.
